purpose: This repository's own changes to the 7.3 tree. It is applied AFTER kernel-patches/7.3 (cnjn's series), and it only contains changes that were measured on this board - values the vendor's own module and this board's flashed image agree on.

patches.what: The IDM register values this board was measured at: the control word's bit 24 and bit 13, the RX retev threshold at +0x0010, the per-queue routing words, the interrupt mask and the source-to-IRQ routing, the descriptor depth, and the words at +0x0490, +0x2c8, +0x124 and +0xbc. The buffer-pool layout is deliberately NOT here: the 7.3 tree has no jumbo pool, so that part needs a patch of its own.

The RX frame lands 0x80 bytes into the buffer the driver hands to the IDM on this board - run 160 printed a whole ARP request and a whole IP/UDP frame at buffer + 0x80 while the driver looked at the head of the page. Four places move together: the page pool's .offset (which is what the cache invalidation and the device-side sync are taken from), the frame's data pointer, the XDP buffer, and the AF_XDP pool size check. The offset is a read-only module parameter so that one boot with zx279133.rx_frame_offset=0 can settle it on the hardware.

IDM+0x100 takes the buffer count encoded, not the count: the vendor's idm_new_bp_update() writes one 0x400 pulse per 1024 buffers and then the remainders. The 7.3 tree writes the count itself and posts 2048 buffers at start-up, which is exactly a multiple of 1024 - so the hardware is told the pool is empty at every boot. The 7.3 tree has a single pool, so only the vendor's normal-pool field is written.

The LAN service grows a control transaction, which is what the 9132 switch driver needs: a control sequence restores the XMAC image and then the XPCS image, and the XPCS restore takes the XMAC lock itself, so the transaction cannot be the XMAC lock. The patch adds the second mutex (lan_control_lock), the two service operations (control_begin and control_end), the parent's implementation of them, the Kconfig entry for the 9132 switch driver and the Makefile line that builds it.
